name: Denmark
headline: Denmark: +3.5% growth in 2025, 1.8% inflation, debt 27% of GDP
sections: Denmark is a $471 billion economy (2025), the world's 36th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.5% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $83K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 18.7% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 1.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.9% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 11.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 27% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 45% in 2020. The general government balance is +2.9% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +12.3% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 129% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.7% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 26% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 82.3 years (2024). Population: 6.0 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
